newsitem.title: CANADA: CWB holds spring wheat yield outlook firm on rains.
newsitem.headline: CWB holds spring wheat yield outlook firm on rains.

text.p: Canadian spring wheat yield forecasts held firm on timely rains on the southeast Prairies, a Canadian Wheat Board weather analyst said.

"We'll have to see what kind of conditions we get further on into July as to whether or not we're going to add any bushels because of the rain but (recent rain) is certainly going to prevent any further deterioration for a while," said Bruce Burnett, weather analyst at the CWB.
Typical yields on Prairie wheat range from 30 to 32 bu/ac but CWB cut them June 11 to 29.5 to 31.5 bu/ac due to dryness on the southeastern Prairies.
Spring wheat was in the heading stage across the Prairies' southern grain belt. That's when the cereals' need for water is most accute.
Southeast Saskatchewan and Manitoba saw 0.8 to 2.8 inches of rain in the past day.

Much of the region's soil held 60 percent or less of its maximum capacity of moisture. Wheat suffers drought stress when its soil has less than 60 percent soil moisture, Environment Canada soil scientist Rick Raddatz said.
